author: Ian Young
title: Vanderburgh County GOP disappointed in Evansville's America 250 preparations - NewsBreak
text:
By Ian Young Ann Powell ,
1 hours ago
EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) — The Vanderburgh County GOP released a statement pushing the city to do more in planning America 250 festivities.
“Evansville played a really big part in the war effort for World War II, and the fact that America 250 seems to be getting glossed over in our city and really just kind of passed by and not recognized the full depth that it should be,” says Vanderburgh County GOP Chairman Khyle Moers.
Vanderburgh County GOP Chairman Khyle Moers says it is sad to see. Moers says the city is prioritizing Pride Month and not America 250.
According to a press release, the republican party says the city council made time to pass a resolution recognizing June as Pride Month. Moers says the focus needs to shift and wants the city to give the same time and attention as Pride Month.
“You see the excitement and momentum building around the country for other celebrations and other forms of recognition for this, and yet Evansville is found to be really not participating in that at all,” says Moers.
River City pride disagrees and says the city is prioritizing America 250.
“I thought it was kind of laughable because we know that the city council, we know that the mayor is both supportive of America,” says Pride Committee Director Ashley Reister. “I thought it was kind of laughable because we know that the city council, we know that the mayor is both supportive of America. To compare it with pride is laughable.”
Democrat Nick Iaccarino sits on the county council and calls the statement petty. He says the city has bigger things to focus on.
“We have too many things that we need to get done,” says City Council Member Nick Iaccarino. “There’s too many opportunities for collaboration, and we need to be seeking those things out instead of just trying to take petty shots.”
One thing both parties can agree on is there is room for both. The city says Mayor Stephanie Terry will issue an official proclamation next week.
The mayor’s office also says there it is working with the Downtown Evansville Economic improvement district and coordinating festivities.
